title: Improving Vitality through Exercise — A Multimodal Prospective Cohort Study on Specialized Inpatient Rehabilitation for Adolescents and Young Adults
summary:
Adolescents and young adults with cancer, heart disease, or lung disease may experience reduced physical performance, fatigue, psychological distress, and limitations in everyday life during and after their illness. Specialized inpatient rehabilitation aims to support their physical and mental health and participation in everyday life. However, little is currently known about how these health domains develop during rehabilitation and in the months following discharge in adolescents and young adults.

The IVE study follows adolescents and young adults aged 16 to 35 years with oncological diseases, cardiological diseases, or cystic fibrosis during specialized inpatient medical rehabilitation at Nachsorgeklinik Tannheim. At the beginning (T0) and end of rehabilitation (T1), physical performance and different aspects of physical and mental health are assessed, including physical function, fatigue, pain, sleep, psychological well-being, and social participation. Additional follow-up assessments are conducted 3 months (FU1), 6 months (FU2), and 12 months (FU3) after rehabilitation discharge.

Exercise and physical activity therapy are part of routine rehabilitation and are not modified by participation in the study. The study investigates how health and physical performance parameters change over time, whether these trajectories differ between the three diagnostic groups, and how exercise-therapy-related factors are associated with these changes. In a subgroup of participants, additional blood samples are analyzed to investigate changes in selected immune parameters.

The findings are intended to improve our understanding of the development of physical and mental health during and after specialized rehabilitation and to contribute to the evidence-based further development of rehabilitation programs for adolescents and young adults with severe chronic diseases.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inpatient medical rehabilitation at Nachsorgeklinik Tannheim; oncological disease, cardiological disease, or cystic fibrosis; participation in routine exercise therapy as part of rehabilitation; capacity to provide informed consent; written informed consent to participate in the study, with additional written informed consent from the legal guardian(s) for minors.
Exclusion criteria:
Failure to meet one or more of the inclusion criteria.
